summary: Reviewed the diff through the hidden-failure / weak-error-handling lens only. The runner's error model is generally sound: exceptions are wrapped in RunnerError and re-raised, failures stop the round and promote nothing, temp files are cleaned up on staging failure, and the catch-all in main() exits non-zero. One finding: the finish_reason check is too narrow and silently accepts abnormal non-length finish reasons (e.g. content_filter), allowing a potentially incomplete or sanitized review to be promoted as complete.

findings.title: finish_reason check accepts content_filter and other abnormal reasons — a filtered/truncated review can be promoted as complete
findings.claim: run_pass only rejects finish_reason == "length". Any other non-"stop" reason — most importantly "content_filter" (the model's output was altered or suppressed by safety filtering) — falls through silently. The body may still be valid JSON that conforms to the schema (e.g., a partial or sanitized findings array), so schema validation does not catch it. The model is signalling that something went wrong with the completion, and the runner ignores that signal, promoting a potentially degraded review as a clean one. This is exactly the silent-degradation pattern this lens targets: code continues in a state where nothing surfaces.
findings.suggestion: Reject any finish_reason that is not "stop" (or at minimum also reject "content_filter" and any unknown reason), raising a RunnerError that names the abnormal reason. If a future API version introduces a new benign reason, it can be allowlisted explicitly at that time.
